title: Swahili: How a Coastal Language Became a National Language
excerpt: Swahili grew from a coastal trading language into the national language of Tanzania and a language spoken by many millions.
body:
## Origins

Swahili is a Bantu language that developed along the East African coast. Contacts with Arabic-speaking traders added many loanwords. The name comes from the Arabic word for "coasts".

## Spread

Trade caravans carried Swahili inland in the 19th century.

## Written

Swahili was written in Arabic script for centuries, later in the Latin alphabet.

## National language

After independence, President Julius Nyerere promoted Swahili as a unifying national language. Today it is the main language in Tanzania, alongside English.

## Today

Swahili is spoken in Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and beyond, by tens of millions as a first or second language.
